newsitem.title: HONDURAS: CIA to release documents about role in Honduras.
newsitem.headline: CIA to release documents about role in Honduras.

text.p: The United States government has promised to release previously classified information about the CIA's anti-insurgency role in Honduras during the 1980s, Honduran officials said on Monday.

Leo Valladares, head of Honduras' government Human Rights Commission, said the information may help determine if the CIA had any role in the disappearance during the decade of 184 people by this Central American nation's security forces.
Valladares released a letter written by U.S. President Bill Clinton to U.S. senators promising the CIA would make the information available beginning in July.

Valladares has pushed the U.S. government to release the information and has said he wants to clear up whether any CIA operatives were involved in the disappearances, which were aimed at suspected leftists.
The CIA and Argentina's military helped train Honduras' military during the 1980s.
Most of the killings took place between 1982-84, when the Honduran military was headed by Gen. Gustavo Alvarez, an ardent anti-communist who was gunned down by leftists in 1990.

The United States helped train Honduras' military during the decade and used land in southern Honduras as a staging area to train right-wing rebels from neighbouring Nicaragua to help overthrow the leftist Sandinista regime in Managua.

In his letter, Clinton said no information would be released that would compromise U.S. national security interests, but added he wanted to release the information to support human rights efforts in the region.
He added that the CIA had already set up an internal investigation into the agency's role in Honduras in the 1980s.

As part of its effort to take the wraps off its most important Cold War actions, the CIA also recently disclosed it had discussed plots to assassinate Guatemalan officials in the 1950s in an effort to turn back communism in that Central American nation.
